source.title: Capacity Control of ReLU Neural Networks by Basis-path Norm
source.authors: Shuxin Zheng; Qi Meng; Hui-Shuai Zhang; Wei Chen; Neng-Hai Yu; Tie-Yan Liu

record.file_problem: The supplied text includes the paper and supplementary material. Figure 2 values are not given numerically in the text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how width and depth relate to empirical generalization error using ReLU MLP sweeps, and tests how a new capacity measure tracks the gap. It is not an explicit replication of the listed studies.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports regularization results on MovieLens-1M and CIFAR-10; these use basis-path regularization, a method not named in the claim versions. The cited results from prior work are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The MNIST width sweep directly tests whether test error continues falling after networks fit the training set. It uses two-hidden-layer ReLU MLPs rather than V2's one-hidden-layer networks and reports improvement followed by slight deterioration.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors derive a generalization bound based on basis-path norm, report that its capacity measure tracks empirical gaps more consistently across network sizes than the compared measures, and report improved held-out performance with basis-path regularization.
record.recipe_differences: Uses ReLU MLPs and width/depth sweeps with SGD on MNIST, measuring training and test error; the paper does not state that it is replicating the cited width study.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test-error trend changes with width and depth: the width sweep has a minimum at 512 units and slight overfitting beyond 1024; the depth sweep has a minimum at 3 layers followed by overfitting.

fits_no_version.finding: Basis-path measure follows the generalization-gap trend across MNIST width and depth sweeps more consistently than the compared norms.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Basis-path capacity measures can track generalization-gap trends across ReLU MLP sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed width 32, test error is lowest with three hidden layers and increases with further depth despite fitting the training data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing depth after fitting the training data can worsen MNIST test performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Networks fit datasets containing 10000 correctly labeled examples plus up to 5000 mislabeled examples; validation error increases as mislabeled examples are added.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ReLU MLPs can fit mixed natural and random labels while generalization worsens with added label corruption.

fits_no_version.finding: Basis-path regularization improves recommendation metrics and CIFAR-10 test performance relative to the reported baselines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suitably tuned basis-path regularization can improve held-out performance.

record.problems: The generalization-measure comparisons are presented in figures without numerical values in the supplied text. Experiments are averaged over 5 trials unless explicitly noted, but uncertainty estimates are not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows omitted. Figure 2 values are unavailable numerically in the supplied text.

untested.parts: No fully random-label training condition or chance-level held-out comparison. Adding up to 5000 mislabeled examples to 10000 correctly labeled examples does not establish the full natural-label versus random-label contrast.
One-hidden-layer networks, downsampled CIFAR-10 and training explicitly to convergence are not tested.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison under matched tuning.
No magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance or comparison of that measure with generalization gaps.
No removal of memorized examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Width verdicts rely on explicit textual descriptions; individual test-error values and uncertainty estimates are unavailable. The wider-network deterioration is slight, and the tested architecture and finite training schedule qualify its applicability to V2.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare separate natural-label and random-label training runs or report held-out accuracy for a fully random-label fit.
The text does not give numerical test errors at individual widths.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks trained from scratch for image generalization.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers and SGD on held-out performance.
Measures basis-path norm and other capacity measures, not magnitude-aware sharpness or weight perturbation tolerance.

rows.subject: MLPs with ReLU, 2 hidden layers
rows.operation_detail: Swept the number of hidden units per layer and measured training and test error on the full MNIST training set.
rows.note: The text says networks fit the training set at widths of at least 32; test error is minimal at 512 and shows slight overfitting beyond 1024. This does not give numeric errors.
rows.check: The aggregate 'reversed' state hides mixed results. Networks fit training data from width 32; test error falls to its minimum at 512, then slightly rises beyond 1024. Split these width ranges into separate rows. Supplementary training details specify SGD, at most 500 epochs, initial learning rate 0.05, exponential decay and batch size 128; convergence is not established.

rows.subject: MLPs with ReLU, 2 hidden layers
rows.stage_stated: trained with SGD; convergence details not stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared basis-path norm, weight norm, path norm and spectral norm with the generalization-error trend across widths.
rows.measure: Trend of capacity measures against generalization error
rows.value: The text says basis-path norm behaves similarly to the generalization-error trend and reaches a minimum at 512; path norm keeps decreasing as width increases.
rows.note: Related capacity-measure evidence, but it does not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness.
rows.check: Basis-path and other norm comparisons do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness. The reported trend is supported by the text, but 'observed' cannot describe an effect in any listed version. Remove the unexplained numbers_found value '1/1'.

rows.subject: MLPs with ReLU, 32 hidden units per layer
rows.stage_stated: trained with SGD; convergence details not stated
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of hidden layers and measured test error and capacity measures.
rows.value: The text says minimal test error is achieved with 3 hidden layers, followed by overfitting as layers increase; basis-path norm nearly matches the generalization error.
rows.note: The text does not enumerate the tested depths or give numerical errors. Basis-path norm is not the measure named in V7.
rows.check: Depth scaling and basis-path norm comparisons test no listed version. Separate test-error and capacity-measure results. Figure 2 identifies tested hidden-layer counts as 2 through 6; the text confirms the minimum at 3 and subsequent overfitting.
